definitions.explanation: Feeling the need or desire to sleep. The state of being tired and wanting to sleep.

examples.japanese: {昨日|きのう}よく{眠|ねむ}れなかったから{眠|ねむ}いです。
examples.english: I'm sleepy because I couldn't sleep well yesterday.

examples.japanese: {朝|あさ}から{眠|ねむ}くて、{仕事|しごと}ができませんでした。
examples.english: I was sleepy since morning and couldn't do my work.

examples.japanese: {子供|こども}たちは{夜|よる}{遅|おそ}くまで{遊|あそ}んでいたので、{今日|きょう}はとても{眠|ねむ}そうな{顔|かお}をしています。
examples.english: The children were playing until late at night, so today they have very sleepy faces.

notes:
{眠|ねむ}い is an i-adjective describing the state of feeling sleepy or drowsy.

FORMS:
- Verb: {眠|ねむ}る (to sleep)
- Noun: {眠|ねむ}り (sleep), {眠|ねむ}さ (sleepiness)
- Adverb: {眠|ねむ}く ({眠|ねむ}くなる = to become sleepy)

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {眠|ねむ}くなる: to become sleepy
- {眠|ねむ}そう: to look sleepy
- とても{眠|ねむ}い: very sleepy
- {眠|ねむ}くて{仕方|しかた}ない: so sleepy I can't help it
- {眠|ねむ}い{目|め}をこする: to rub sleepy eyes

KANJI COMPOUNDS:
- {睡眠|すいみん}: sleep (formal)
- {睡眠不足|すいみんぶそく}: lack of sleep
- {仮眠|かみん}: nap
- {安眠|あんみん}: restful sleep

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {疲|つか}れた: tired (physical exhaustion)
- だるい: sluggish, listless
- {眠|ねむ}たい: sleepy (variant, slightly more casual)

NOTE:
{眠|ねむ}い specifically describes wanting to sleep, while {疲|つか}れた is about physical/mental exhaustion. You can be {疲|つか}れた without being {眠|ねむ}い, and vice versa.
